- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for negative sentiment.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 20–40% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 15–30% if sentiment drops below 0.33 after prior peak.
- For 30-day forecasts, model exhibits mean reversion bias — overestimates in early days, underestimates in late days; apply a “midpoint correction”: average last 7–10 days of history for baseline, then adjust ±15% based on sentiment trend.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to underperform; increase forecast by 5–15% to account for low conviction.
- Model often ignores sentiment in early forecast windows (first 5–7 days); apply “sentiment lag” rule: if sentiment > 0.67 in last 3 days, adjust forecast for next 7 days upward by 5–10%.
